request.spec:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was
cleared).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was
cleared).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People now have a contact, and all 4 Playwright tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V61__person_contact.sql`, adds a `contact` column to `person`. A unique index on sheet + contact stops two people on the same sheet having the same contact. People with no contact don't clash.
- **Server:**
  - The server trims and lower-cases the contact; a blank one is saved as none.
  - Adding or editing a person with a contact another person on the sheet already has is refused, and nothing is saved.
  - `PERSON_ADDED` ends with `contact=<contact>` when the form gave one.
  - `PERSON_EDITED` ends with `contact=<contact>` when the contact changed, or `contact=` when it was cleared.
  - Bulk grading keeps each person's contact as it is.
- **Front end:** the person form has a `person-form-contact` field, which the editor fills in when opened. Each row shows the contact in a `person-contact` cell.

My first version also checked for duplicate contacts in the browser before saving. It broke the two-user step: the refusal never reached the server, so the user's out-of-date copy of the person wasn't refreshed and their next edit failed. I removed that check, so only the server decides now.

One cosmetic gap: a duplicate name and a duplicate contact are both refused the same way, so the form shows the same message for either: "That name or contact is already in use on this sheet."
